about.title: About Stock Calculator - Investment Return Analysis Tool
about.description: The Stock Calculator is a stock investment analysis tool designed to help you calculate returns, gains, losses, and performance metrics for individual stock investments. This calculator uses purchase prices, selling prices, dividends, and time periods to estimate total returns and annualized performance. Whether you're tracking existing investments or planning stock purchases, this tool provides formula-based stock return calculations.

faq.q: How do I calculate stock returns?
faq.a: Total return = (Ending Value + Dividends - Beginning Value) / Beginning Value. Include all dividends received and subtract transaction costs for a more complete net return estimate. Use annualized returns for comparing different time periods.

faq.q: What's the difference between realized and unrealized gains?
faq.a: Realized gains occur when you sell stock for more than you paid. Unrealized gains are 'paper profits' on stocks you still own. Only realized gains are taxable, and tax rates depend on holding period (short vs. long-term).

faq.q: How do dividends affect stock returns?
faq.a: Dividends are part of total return and should be included in performance calculations. Dividend yield = Annual Dividends / Stock Price. Reinvested dividends compound returns over time through additional share purchases.

faq.q: What costs should I include in stock calculations?
faq.a: Include all transaction costs: brokerage commissions, SEC fees, exchange fees, and any account maintenance fees. These costs reduce your net returns and should be factored into performance analysis.
